trial_court: Additional District Judge, Kangra at Dharamshala, Hindu Marriage petition No. 265 of 2016
facts_of_case: The husband preferred an application under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act for maintenance pendente lite and litigation expenses. The trial court allowed the application and granted a sum of Rs. 10,000/- as per-mensem maintenance and Rs. 20,000/- as litigation expenses.

legal_principles.principle: The court cannot be constrained to conclude a sum of maintenance pendente lite without considering the income drawn by the respondent.
legal_principles.held: yet hence the afore averment remained un-cast in the application, rather the respondent herein visibly concealed the afore factum, hence, the learned Additional District Judge, could not, prima-facie, be constrained to conclude that a sum of Rs. 10,000/- per-mensem, is the determinable amount towards the per-mensem maintenance pendente lite, vis-à-vis, the respondent herein.

legal_principles.principle: The court must bear in mind the uncontested factum while rendering an order.
legal_principles.held: 4. The learned Additional District Judge, (1), Kangra at Dharamshala, in the impugned order, while bearing in mind the afore facet, vis-à-vis, the salary drawn by, the petitioner herein, and, vis-à-vis, the fellowship, drawn by the respondent herein from her afore avocation, ...

legal_principles.principle: The court must apply the requisite statutory principles while rendering an order.
legal_principles.held: 6. In aftermath, with the learned Additional District Judge, (1), Kangra at Dharamshala, failing to bear in mind the, requisite statutory principles, cast in Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, ...

outcome.final_order: The final order was in favour of the respondent wife, confirming the trial court's decision on maintenance pendente lite and litigation expenses.
